hero.sub: An alarm sounding in the garden unit, a basement toilet that won't drain or a sewer smell. We repair and replace ejector pumps in Ravenswood homes and two-flats. Our office is on Ravenswood Avenue. Open 24/7.

blocks.body: Fixtures below the sewer line, like a garden unit bathroom or a basement laundry, drain into a sealed basin. The ejector pump lifts that wastewater into the main line. A float starts it and a check valve keeps water from falling back. If one part fails, the fixtures back up.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber working on the discharge pipe of a basement sump pump

blocks.h2: Planning Plumbing for a Garden Unit Conversion
blocks.body: Turning a Ravenswood basement into a garden apartment usually means a bathroom, a kitchen and laundry below the sewer line. That plumbing needs an ejector pump, a sealed basin, proper venting and an alarm. We size the pump for every fixture it serves and plan where the basin goes, ideally where it can be reached for service. It's a lot easier to plan this before the drywall goes up.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of Ejector Pump Work
blocks.body: Replacing just the pump is the simplest job. A new basin, check valve, vent work or an alarm adds to it. Access under a finished floor matters too. We inspect and quote a flat price.

items.q: The garden unit alarm is on. What now?
items.preview: Stop using basement fixtures and call us.
items.answer: Stop using every fixture that drains to the basin and call us right away.

items.q: How long do ejector pumps last?

items.q: Why does it smell like sewer downstairs?
items.preview: A seal, vent or dry trap.
